title: Tessel: Boosting Distributed Execution of Large DNN Models via Flexible Schedule Search
problem: Distributed DNN execution requires carefully planned schedules across multiple devices, but existing predefined schedules do not fully exploit emerging operator placement strategies and handcrafting efficient schedules is challenging due to large search spaces.
motivation: Increasingly complex DNN models require distributed execution across multiple devices, necessitating automated methods to find optimal execution schedules for training and inference.
method: Tessel employs a two-phase schedule search approach: (1) repetend construction that exploits repetitive patterns in efficient schedules across data inputs to reduce search costs, and (2) schedule completion. The system explores schedules for various operator placement strategies to optimize both training and inference performance.
key_novelty: Tessel leverages the insight that efficient execution schedules exhibit repetitive patterns (repetends) across different data inputs to dramatically reduce schedule search space and computational cost.
contributions: Automated schedule search system (Tessel) for distributed DNN training and inference
Two-phase approach combining repetend construction and schedule completion to reduce search overhead
Support for flexible operator placement strategies in distributed execution
Achieves up to 5.5x training speedup and 38% inference latency reduction on representative DNNs
primary_theme: automated schedule search for distributed DNN execution
